action: Place probe in transverse position. Immediately identify the target vessel.
interpretation: Identify a pulsatile aorta immediately upon placing the probe.

action: Assess the posterior landmarks. Verify depth settings.
interpretation: Identify the vertebral shadow and the vertebral body at a depth of approximately 10 centimeters.

action: Freeze the image upon obtaining a clear view. Prepare to measure.
interpretation: View is identified. Plan to measure the aortic diameter from outer wall to outer wall.

action: Activate calipers. Place calipers on the outer walls of the aorta.
interpretation: Positioning calipers for measurement.

action: Read the measurement on the screen.
interpretation: The diameter is 2.6 centimeters, which is a normal finding.

action: Adjust caliper placement if necessary to capture the full width.
interpretation: Acknowledge slight overestimation of the size. Reasoning: It is clinically safer to overestimate than underestimate the aorta.

action: Unfreeze the image. Resume scanning.
interpretation: Continuing the scan.

action: Drag the probe inferiorly towards the feet. Maintain the same transverse orientation.
interpretation: Scanning down the length of the aorta.

action: Apply constant, firm pressure. Fan the probe gently to displace obstruction.
interpretation: Bowel gas is obscuring the view and causing loss of aortic visualization. Pressure and fanning are used to move the gas around.

action: Decrease the depth setting.
interpretation: Optimizing the image by reducing depth.

action: Inspect the right side of the screen.
interpretation: Visualize the aorta located on the right side of the screen.

action: Inspect the left side of the screen and posterior field.
interpretation: Visualize the IVC partially on the left side of the screen and identify the vertebral shadow again.

action: Freeze image (optional). Measure the aorta at this level.
interpretation: Process can be repeated to document diameter at this level.

action: Drag the probe downward towards the distal aorta, positioning just above the umbilicus. Continue until vessel splits.
interpretation: Tracking the aorta distally to locate the bifurcation.

action: Hold position at the split.
interpretation: Visualize the bifurcation point.

action: Fan the probe back and forth.
interpretation: Fanning clarifies the structure so it is visible on the screen.

action: Analyze anatomical relationship on screen.
interpretation: IVC is located on the left side of the screen; the bifurcation is on the right side.

action: Prepare to transition to the sagittal plane. Plan to scan suprarenal and infrarenal areas.
interpretation: Objective is to acquire the aorta in the sagittal plane.

action: Slide the probe to center the aorta on the screen.
interpretation: Centering the vessel for rotation.

action: Align the vessel with the posterior landmark.
interpretation: The aorta is situated right above the vertebral shadow.

action: Use two hands. Rotate the probe 90 degrees so the marker points towards the patient's head. Maintain visualization of the aorta throughout the rotation.
interpretation: Transitioning to longitudinal view while keeping the target in sight.

action: Scan the aorta in sagittal plane completely.
interpretation: Reasoning: This view ensures detection of saccular aneurysms, which can be easily missed if skipping through transverse views.

action: Establish the longitudinal view.
interpretation: Confirm view of the aorta in the sagittal plane.

action: Drag the probe inferiorly.
interpretation: Visualize the infrarenal aorta in the sagittal plane.

action: Instruct patient to bend knees. Press downward firmly. Wait for bowel gas to displace.
interpretation: Troubleshooting tip: These actions help clear bowel gas. Acknowledge that distinguishing IVC from Aorta can be confusing in the sagittal plane.

action: Slide the probe towards the patient's right.
interpretation: This maneuver should isolate the IVC.

action: Identify IVC, then slide the probe back to the patient's left.
interpretation: Confirm the first vessel is the IVC. Confirm the vessel on the left is the Aorta.

action: Use this sweep to verify anatomy.
interpretation: This serves as a quick confirmation method to ensure the correct vessel is being targeted.
